claim_verdicts.source: Execution: dart run scratchpad/late_test.dart, Dart SDK 3.13.2 (stable, flutter 3.47.2)

issues.text: 'spinner' is UI jargon not in known_vocab and not defined. I can guess it means some loading picture, but I have not been told. It appears in the Try-it question and again in quiz q3 option a, where I must judge it.
issues.quote: Why could `LoginScreen` not be a StatelessWidget that shows a spinner while signing in?
issues.fix: Replace 'a spinner' with 'a loading indicator' in the Try-it question and in q3 option a (EN and VI).

issues.text: 'fields' here means the two text boxes on the login form, but in this lesson 'fields' always meant variables stored in the `State`. I first read it as 'two State fields' and could not tell which two.
issues.quote: what is typed in the two fields
issues.fix: Replace 'what is typed in the two fields' with 'what is typed in the email and password boxes'.

issues.text: The prose says the screen replaces `_products` when the refresh button is pressed, but the code block stops at `initState`, so I cannot find that line and have to take it on trust. Same for the `build` that reads `_products`.
issues.quote: And when the user presses the refresh button, the screen replaces `_products` with a new load by itself
issues.fix: Add 'further down in the same file (not shown here)' after 'the screen replaces `_products` with a new load by itself'.

issues.text: The block uses `late` and `super.initState()`; the prose explains `initState` but not these. Coming from C#, I do not know what `late` means and wonder if it matters for keeping `_products`.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: '`late` only tells Dart the field is set before it is first read, here in `initState`; ignore it for now.'

issues.text: The diagram has an arrow from 'inputs from the parent' to StatefulWidget, but section 4's prose only says a StatefulWidget remembers things 'without anyone passing it a new value', and Core concepts says 'without new values passed in from outside'. I first thought a StatefulWidget takes no inputs; only section 5 (`apiClient`) corrects that.
issues.quote: without anyone passing it a new value
issues.fix: In section 4, add one sentence: 'A StatefulWidget still receives inputs from its parent like any widget; the `State` holds what it must remember on top of them.'

issues.text: 'a second object ... that you must keep correct' — I do not know what keeping a `State` correct means or what mistakes it could have; the lesson never shows one. The same vague phrase is the key of quiz q5.
issues.quote: a second object that Flutter keeps alive and that you must keep correct
issues.fix: Replace 'that you must keep correct' with 'whose fields you must set and update yourself'.

issues.text: The correction relies on product rows and their `Text`, which this lesson never shows. I have to believe that rows are built from `Text` widgets and that they show a price.
issues.quote: Each product's `Text` is stateless, yet the rows show different names, and a row would show a new price if the list were built again with new data.
issues.fix: Add 'in `ProductListScreen`'s list' after 'Each product's `Text`', so I know where to look in the file I already opened.

issues.text: Connections says a `State` object provides `context` and `mounted`; the lesson body never says this, so it is a new idea appearing only in a link line.
issues.quote: the `context` and `mounted` that a `State` object provides.

issues.text: Option d 'the app shell' — I know 'shell' only as a command-line program, so I first read this as a terminal. The explanation reveals it means `DonHangApp`.
issues.quote: The app shell that sets the title and first screen
issues.fix: Replace with 'The top-level app widget that sets the title and first screen' (EN and VI).

issues.text: The correct option is almost the lesson's own sentence ('comes with a separate `State` object ... Flutter creates the `State` once, keeps it'), so I can match words instead of understanding.
issues.quote: In a separate `State` object Flutter keeps alive
issues.fix: Reword to 'In an object Flutter creates once and reuses while the widget is on screen'.

issues.text: q2 option c repeats the misconception correction word for word ('its parent can build it again with new inputs'); q5 option c repeats 'adds a second object ... keep correct' and is also clearly the longest option. Both are answerable by matching text.
issues.quote: False, because its parent can build it again with new inputs.
issues.fix: Paraphrase both keys, e.g. q2c 'False, because what it shows follows the values it is given each time', and shorten q5c to the length of the other options.

skipped_steps: Refresh replacing `_products` is asserted but the code for it is outside the shown block.
